groups.title: Who controls each money function
groups.summary: These studies identify the institutions and decision rights behind issuing dollars, operating payment services, overseeing the system and changing its rules. Read them together to locate the responsible actor and distinguish the different kinds of power.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep the Board, each Reserve Bank, the FOMC, shared services, auditors, Congress, Treasury and private utilities separate. Appointment, audit, budget approval and operating command are different powers.

groups.title: Which record controls a tokenized claim
groups.summary: These studies follow the legal claim, ownership or position record, custody and correction rules behind a token. They share questions about which record controls and who is accountable when records disagree.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep issuer ownership, Cede registration, DTC participant entitlements, downstream customer rights, wallet access and chain transfers separate. Rule approval does not establish an operating launch.

groups.title: Who supplies money, collateral and loss protection
groups.summary: These studies trace funding, collateral, obligations and loss through a transaction. Read them together to distinguish the party supplying cash from the party holding collateral, owing repayment or bearing a default loss.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep the FICC service, cash investor, sponsor, BNY custody, Fed proposal and each transaction separate. Shared branding or custody does not prove an XRP-funded repo or connect an unproved XRP claim to an operating transaction.

groups.title: From legal permission to an operating crypto service
groups.summary: These studies ask what a particular permission allows, who holds it and which further evidence would show a service operating. The shared sequence connects legal instruments to named products and operating receipts while preserving each jurisdiction’s rules.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep charters, deposit-taking, stablecoin issuer authority, exchange or DCO registration, exemptions, staff positions, proposals, statutes, final rules, first trades and legal finality separate. One permission is not a general approval of crypto activities.

groups.title: From payment event to books and assurance
groups.summary: These studies follow an authorized event through payment, operational records, accounting and assurance. Read them together to identify the handoffs and the different authorities, judgments and evidence requirements.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep technical atomic execution, legal discharge, accounting recognition and measurement, double-entry books, attestations, auditor judgment and remedies separate. Visibility to an operator is not public transparency.

groups.title: Payment checks, eligibility and fraud data
groups.summary: These studies follow the checks and data handoffs around public payments. Use them together to identify who supplies a signal, who may use it and who makes the program or payment decision.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep screening matches, identity evidence, eligibility decisions, agency adverse action, MOU authority, actual data exchange, payment stops and proven fraud separate; sharing data does not merge agencies.

groups.title: Public funding from authority to recipient
groups.summary: These studies follow public funding from legal authority through awards, payments and downstream use. The worked cases show which records connect those stages and where a public link is still missing.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep appropriations, requests, rescission proposals, obligations, federal outlays, state receipts, subawards, nonprofit-reported revenue, project entities and demonstrated results separate; a missing public join stays missing.

groups.title: Science programs from selection to operation
groups.summary: These studies follow the different finance, security and qualification steps between a science or industrial plan and accepted operation. Each program, technology and project keeps its own actors and evidence.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep doctrine, selection, appropriation, contract, company commitment, facility, license, accepted part, workload and operation separate; do not add different Genesis cohorts or measured units into one current total.

groups.title: Energy and logistics routes
groups.summary: These studies connect named physical routes and projects to the owners, permissions, payments and operating evidence that support them. Use the globe for route context and the individual views for each legal or project question.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep cargo, ownership, sanctions permission, invoice currency, bank payment, receipt, capacity orders, delivered equipment and operating power separate; nearby or co-located functions do not establish one commercial transaction.

groups.title: International institutions and national change
groups.summary: These studies distinguish an international institution’s powers and decisions from the national actions needed to change money, rules or operating arrangements. The country and monetary views show which particular function is changing.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep treaty authority, forum agendas, recommendations, national implementation, membership, assessments, funding shares, votes, loan conditions and operating substitution separate; percentages with different denominators are not interchangeable.

groups.title: Country institutions, money and cross-border links
groups.summary: These studies ask how a country’s own institutions, claims and balance sheets connect to money, trade and cross-border relationships. They provide country introductions and narrower tests of a named mechanism.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep each country’s legal forms and jurisdictions intact. IMF classifications, currency windows, market moves, proposals and operating evidence are different measures; a proposed connection remains a hypothesis until its own evidence supports it.

groups.title: Government maps, source checks and confirmed changes
groups.summary: These views help readers move from a government body or source check to the dated evidence for a change. The broad map provides entrances; each campaign and subject study retains its own findings and cutoff.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep map coverage, website access, unreviewed candidates, legal instruments, implementation and observed outcomes separate. A later sweep does not update an older campaign’s evidence date, and a monitor lead does not become a finding by appearing here.

groups.title: Legal powers, personnel, court procedure and operation
groups.summary: These studies identify who holds a power, which instrument exercises it, what courts have done and what evidence shows in operation. The broad collections lead to separate case and instrument maps.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep statutes, offices, agency legal existence, operating functions, removal powers, force authorization, court remedies and observed conduct separate. A stay is a procedural event, not a merits holding; source-date conflicts must be resolved before making a current-state claim.

groups.title: Official records, public claims and their limits
groups.summary: These views help readers move from a speech, release or source collection to the exact record behind a claim. Some compare release methods; others provide a dated corpus or a close reading of one event.
groups.keep_distinct: Keep statements, testimony, agency conclusions, legal effect, independent corroboration, causal claims and adjudication separate. Similar release methods do not establish shared actors, causes or outcomes across the subjects.

rule: The reviewed groups are contextual connections. Standalone studies remain first-class.
